:::{#exm-fitting-procedure}
#### Inputs of two fitting procedures

Least-squares polynomial fitting of degree $\polydeg$ has these inputs:

- data: the observations the polynomial is fitted to;
- [model family](#def-model-family): the polynomials of degree at most $\polydeg$;
- [objective function](#def-objective-function): the sum of squared errors over those observations;
- [optimization algorithm](#def-optimization-algorithm): solving the normal equations, which finds the unique minimizer exactly;
- [random seed](#def-random-seed): none, since nothing is random;
- [tuning parameter](#def-tuning-parameter): the degree $\polydeg$;
- preprocessing: none.

Because the minimizer is unique and exact, the family, the data and the objective already determine the fitted rule.

A random forest of regression trees is different:

- data: the observations the trees are grown on;
- model family: averages of regression trees;
- objective function: the sum of squared errors within each tree's leaves;
- optimization algorithm: greedy splitting of the covariate space, tree by tree;
- random seed: fixes which observations and covariates each tree uses;
- tuning parameters: the number of trees and the minimum leaf size;
- preprocessing: none.

Here the greedy search finds no exact minimizer,
so two seeds give different fitted rules from the same data.

:::
